timeline.label: Q3 FY2026 10-Q: revenue $14.9B for the quarter; cash $7.1B and long-term debt $19.4B anchor the valuation proof.
FY2025: $6.0B buybacks and $6.4B dividends; normalized owner earnings $13.3B (OCF minus capex).
FY2025 10-K filed: consolidated revenue $56.7B; net income $10.2B; three geographic segments.
2025 proxy documents board composition and executive compensation under CEO Charles Robbins.
Splunk acquisition closed, expanding observability and recurring software mix within Cisco's security and networking stack.
FY2024 revenue $53.8B; baseline year before full Splunk contribution in FY2025.
Activist DFAN14A proxy solicitation filings on record (multiple exhibits); context for capital-return pressure.
Elliott Management SC 13D/A discloses activist stake; historical catalyst for operating and capital-allocation review.
Shift toward software and subscription revenue (Cisco Plus, security bundles) reduces pure hardware cyclicality.
Charles Robbins succeeded John Chambers as CEO; capital allocation and portfolio simplification under new leadership.

industry.structure: Global enterprise networking and security oligopoly with high switching costs on installed bases; competition from white-box vendors, cloud-native security, and hyperscaler self-build networking.
industry.share_shift: Cisco gains when enterprises consolidate vendors for secure networking; loses share when cloud workloads bypass traditional hardware or when price-sensitive buyers adopt merchant silicon.
industry.trend: AI-ready data-center networking, subscription software (Splunk observability), and recurring security attach are growing mix drivers; capital spending remains light relative to cash generation.
